symptom: A microflow created over --mcp (Studio Pro PED, 11.15.0-rc.4) read back with every sequence flow 1 -> 3: a CASE built with `@anchor(from: bottom, Approved: (from: right), (empty): (from: bottom, to: top))` lost all three anchors and the merge's bottom exit. A script with any `@annotation` failed the create outright: `microflow object type *microflows.Annotation is not yet supported by the MCP backend`.
cause: buildFlowDocContent mapped a SequenceFlow to originId/destinationId/caseValue only, so Studio Pro applied its right -> left default; the splice (flowPatchOps) already sent originConnectionSide/destinationConnectionSide. mapObjectTree had no Annotation case and ObjectCollection.AnnotationFlows was never read. The splice's note line used originId/destinationId, the SequenceFlow constructor's keys. PED's AnnotationFlow is an element type that takes origin/destination plus the required originConnectionIndex/destinationConnectionIndex, and refuses the constructor keys with `"/origin":"Expected reference (string), got undefined"`. That bug was hidden because the note was refused before its line was mapped.
file: mdl/backend/mcp/microflow.go (buildFlowDocContent, mapObjectTree, setPEDSides, pedAnnotationFlow, adaptMicroflowSkeleton, CreateMicroflow), mdl/backend/mcp/microflow_mutator.go (flowPatchOps), sdk/microflows/microflows.go (AnnotationFlow.SidesOrDefault)
insight: Compare engines, not shapes: run the same script through the modelsdk engine and over --mcp, then diff each flow's (origin, destination, sides) after resolving PED's $id(/objectCollection/objects/N) references to positions. That diff covered all 10 flows (identical after the fix, every one 1 -> 3 before) and settled the bug faster than reading either writer. Read ped_get_schema per element type: 'constructor type' and 'element type' differ in key names (originId vs origin) for what looks like the same flow list. PED's read-back omits a property at its default, so a missing connection index means 0 (Top), not absent. The pre-11.14 constructor cannot type a flow, so notes are refused there: an untyped note line would be read as a SequenceFlow. Within one update PED stores an AnnotationFlow after a SequenceFlow added later, so the splice adds its note lines last; otherwise its index-addressed sets on the new sequence flow would point at the wrong flow. Still open: ALTER insert over MCP on 11.15 fails whenever it sets line/<end>ControlVector on a flow added in the same update (`undefined is not an object (evaluating 'u.$Type')`), with or without a note.
